# Expo HAS CHANGED

Read the versioned docs at https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v57.0.0/ before writing Expo code.

This file holds only the always-on rules, each in a few lines with a pointer: the long text lives in `docs/solutions/` and is never pasted back here (the byte budget of `wf check --budget` enforces it). Area how-to is in nested `AGENTS.md` files that load under `frontend/mla-tamagui/`, `frontend/mla-tamagui/features/`, `infra/oracle-cloud/`, `.agents/`. Vocabulary: `CONCEPTS.md`. Open debt: `docs/known-gaps.md`.

## Links

Every URL or deep link shared with the user is a markdown link with a short label, never bare. The phone link is an EAS Update (the `### EAS Update` link of the CI run summary, or what `wf ship eas --latest` / `--initial-route <route>` prints), never a live Metro. The `exp://` rule and the details: `docs/solutions/workflow/phone-and-deep-links.md`.

## Delegate mechanical work to cheap models

`.claude/rules/delegation.md` has the routing table. Whole workflows go to opencode: `/cheap <task>`, `wf offload ask "<prompt>"`, `wf offload ask --batch`, `wf offload plan <slug>`, or the `delegate` MCP tool. Trivial steps (one known file, at most 10 lines, a single Read or Grep) stay direct. Never delegate through the `Agent` tool.

## Act, don't ask

Before asking the user for anything, try it yourself; ask only after a concrete attempt failed with a real error. Look for the credential (`bws secret list`, `env`, `~/.oci`, `~/.ssh`), install the missing tool (`mise`, `pip3`). Two real limits: GitHub Actions secrets (CI secrets live in Bitwarden) and SSH to the VM (use `vm-ops-api`, `wf vm net up`). Mint credentials yourself; ask only for what authenticates a person, once, with the exact command. The user works from a phone: a link beats a handover, `https://` beats a custom scheme, say when a step needs a desktop.

## Code architecture

Ports and adapters, one shape per package type: dependencies point inward to a pure core (`domain/` does no I/O), the core owns its ports, adapters implement them, one composition root wires them. A feature owns its slice in `frontend/mla-tamagui/features/<name>`; Rust services are `core`/`rs` crate pairs; `clis/wf` is split by concept into crates (`wf` is only the router). Shapes, the crate list and the checks (`pnpm run arch:services`, `pnpm --filter mla-tamagui run arch`): `docs/solutions/architecture/hexagonal-architecture-by-package-type.md` and `docs/solutions/architecture/code-architecture-rules.md`.

## Comments

Prefer none. Comment only a non-obvious why, 2 lines max.

## Capability goes in a `clis/*` package surfaced via `wf`, never `scripts/`

Search `wf --help` first. A wrapper script that sets up env or flags is a smell; fix the `wf` command.

## CI runs on the VM

Pushing to `dev` runs one pipeline, the reusable `pipeline.yml`: `deploy.yml` ("CI (self-hosted)") calls it on the VM's own Actions runner (one job at a time), `ci-hosted.yml` on GitHub-hosted runners; every test stage replays through the Nx cache. The local gate is lefthook pre-commit (`wf check --staged`): a red hook is the failure to fix, never to bypass. Production ships only by a push to `dev`: CI builds the images on its runner and the legs redeploy that tag (`wf ship --redeploy-only`); agent sessions cannot dispatch workflows and nothing else builds a production image. Every stage, the deploy flow, the hand-deployed apps and the record triggers: `docs/solutions/ci/ci-pipeline-on-the-vm.md`.

## Never wait on CI

A running or queued CI run is never a reason to stop or idle: take the next item of the goal at once. Watch a run with one background Monitor; never poll, `sleep` or end a turn to wait. Push further commits while a run is queued (a newer push supersedes it); a red run is one more item of work. Hold a push only for a conflict with half-finished work in the tree.

## Parallel agents in the sandbox

Work independent issue items in parallel, one agent per git worktree that never pushes or touches the main checkout; every `cargo`, `pnpm` test and `wf check|test` command runs as `flock /tmp/cargo.lock <command>`; stop and report at under 1.2 GB free. Details: `docs/solutions/workflow/parallel-agents-in-the-sandbox.md`.

## Land on dev

Work autonomously on the `dev` trunk, never a session branch; never delete a branch. Before any work bring `dev` to parity with `main` (`docs/solutions/workflow/dev-parity-with-main.md`); land with `git fetch origin dev && git rebase origin/dev` (never over a merge of `main`), the lefthook suite, push. Deploy is automatic on push to `dev`; never call `/redeploy` by hand. When the open `dev` → `main` PR is merged or closed, open a new one titled exactly `dev → main` with the body exactly ``This is `dev` ``. The rest: `docs/solutions/workflow/land-on-dev.md`.

## Benchmarks: always, and as cheap as still meaningful

Every new or changed skill, hook, harness lever or workflow gets a cheap benchmark before it ships (`wf offload ask --stats`, `--savings`; n=1 first, the mock opencode where the model does not matter); log the numbers and the decision in `docs/audits/2026-09-02-token-diet-decision-log.md`.

## Tests: what counts as verification

Say which type ran (runbook, browser/Android e2e, deployment verification, integration, flow, unit; if only unit, say so plainly): `docs/solutions/testing/verification-ladder.md`. Every recordable test run publishes a recording, every harness run ends with a report, every CI test run publishes a run bundle (`wf test publish`); Given/When/Then in every test; test behavior, never the implementation; every `wf` verb answers an agent in one call with stable JSON. Visually verify anything visual and show it via `SendUserFile`. Mobile definition of done: an EAS Update (`wf ship eas --initial-route <route>`). All rules: `docs/solutions/testing/verification-rules.md`.

## The Oracle Cloud VM

One Always-Free A1 VM (`main`) runs every app; deploy = a CI leg (`wf ship`, then a `vm-ops-api` redeploy); no SSH. Downtime is never a concern; recoverability without a human is (check tfstate before destroying); never destroy vault secrets or tfstate history. Recreating an Always-Free instance via Terraform is pre-authorized. Details: `infra/oracle-cloud/AGENTS.md`.

## Secrets

Never in committed files. `.env.defaults` is committed non-secret config; `.env` is generated (`wf secret sync-env --for <app> --base .env.defaults`). `clis/secrets/src/data/registry.json` is the source of truth for keys: add the entry before introducing a secret, never fabricate a value. opencode never holds an Anthropic credential.

## Scheduled tasks are clocks

Name them `<What> clock (<cadence>)` and fire a one-sentence tick into the persistent `schedules` session (`create_trigger` with `persistent_session_id`), never a standalone prompt that starts a fresh session: `docs/solutions/workflow/scheduled-task-clocks.md`.

## Generated agent config

`.agents/` is the only source (`instructions/`, `config/*.json`, `commands/`, `skills/`, `setup.sh`). Never edit a generated file (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.opencode/commands`, `opencode.json`, `.mcp.json`); edit the source, then `pnpm run sync:agent-config` (`sync:check` fails on drift). Details: `.agents/AGENTS.md`.

## Tooling rules that bite

- The emulator runs only in CI: never `wf android start-device|stop-device|lease` or a device-driving verb by hand; device evidence is the CI Android job's bundles.
- `wf` only, never raw `simctl`; browser verification is `wf browser` against a local `expo export --platform web` (`wf test prepare --web`).
- RTK: call `rtk <tool>` directly; never append `| head`, `| tail` or `| cat` (the hook blocks it and names the command): `docs/solutions/tooling-decisions/rtk-usage.md`.
- Background processes: keep the PID from launch (`setsid nohup … & echo $! > .agents/tmp/<name>.pid`); `pgrep -f`/`pkill -f` match your own shell.
- Long cross-builds run in the background with raw output to a log file.
- Logging: no `console.*`; `Logger.*` (static event names, variables as fields); catch blocks log or rethrow; a log line counts only when a query at the sink returns it.
- Dependencies: vet maintenance, provenance, license, footprint; run `pnpm run audit`.
- GitHub: `gh` is provisioned at session start; fall back to the GitHub MCP tools if missing.
- Spawning Claude Code Remote sessions: target the "No holds barred" environment via `list_environments`.
- UI iteration hold: when asked to verify a UI change, make no edits until the user says "resume edits".
- Submodules: `references/` holds shallow reference-only submodules; `pnpm run submodule:init` when needed.
